sections.overview: Lethrinus erythracanthus Valenciennes, 1830 is a widely distributed Indo-Pacific emperor fish, recorded from East Africa to the central Pacific.
sections.identification: Adults are brown to dark grey with variable pale and dark markings; small orange cheek spots and orange-toned fins are characteristic, and the species can reach 70 cm.
sections.habitat: It uses deep lagoons, channels, outer reef slopes and neighbouring soft bottoms, generally at 20–120 m in the FAO account.
sections.diet: Its recorded prey include echinoderms, crustaceans and molluscs; these are mostly bottom-dwelling invertebrates.
sections.behavior: It is often solitary by day, resting in or near ledges and caves on reefs.
sections.reproduction: The species accounts consulted do not provide a confirmed spawning season.
sections.ecology: Older taxonomic treatments confused it with Lethrinus erythropterus and L. kallopterus; the FAO catalogue recognizes L. erythracanthus as distinct based on diagnostic colour patterns and anatomical characters.
sections.conservation: FishBase lists a 2015 IUCN assessment of Least Concern; this dated category alone does not indicate current abundance at a particular reef.

sources.title: Lethrinus erythracanthus — Coastal Fishes of the Western Indian Ocean, vol. 3
